solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Administrative record of car manufacturer having race on section of track

parts.note: Audi is the German car maker
the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
a rail is one length of railway track

explanation.surface: Someone files a report on a car maker that has a race on part of a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit trail is the chronological log of transactions kept so that accounts can be checked by an auditor.

clue.text: Starter home with no roof covered by additional credit

parts.note: new can mean further or additional, as in a new supply

indicators.note: one piece covered by another sits inside it, here between the halves of the outer pair

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof of a word is its top letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: home taken as the plain word

explanation.surface: A first-time buyer's house without a roof is financed by extra borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, but it means a beginner; 'with no roof' drops the top letter, since in a down entry the roof is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is someone just starting out somewhere, a beginner or starter.

clue.text: On which bouncers work out

parts.note: bouncers suggests nightclub doormen at the gym, but here they are people bouncing up and down for exercise

explanation.walkthrough: Bouncers reads as doormen and work out as a gym session; really it is anyone who bounces, exercising on a springy mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprung canvas frame is the apparatus that people jump up and down on for exercise or fun.

clue.text: Villain, one that has gone

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
ago describes time that has passed, as in years ago

explanation.surface: A bad guy, one who has already left.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's schemer in Othello is literature's archetypal villain.

clue.text: Valley in which dead white European male is ultimately read

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the four words that follow it

explanation.surface: A valley where a dead white European male author is finally read.
explanation.definitionFit: A dene is a narrow wooded valley, a word common in northern English place names.

clue.text: Topless cruel woman and man briefly had urges

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so topless drops it

parts.note: a malicious woman is insultingly called a bitch
Ed is a short form of the man's name Edward

explanation.surface: A topless spiteful woman and a man briefly felt urges.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the top is the first letter, so 'Topless' drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have itched for something is to have longed or had an urge to do it.

clue.text: Might it control warmth of heartless little beast?

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word for the animal

parts.note: a stoat is a small weasel-like mammal

explanation.surface: A question about whether a small creature without a heart could regulate heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central O out of STOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is the short form of thermostat, the device that regulates heating.

clue.text: Contemplation of setter about himself and solvers?

indicators.note: about means round, so the setter's word wraps the other

parts.note: a setter refers to himself as me
the setter together with the solvers make us

explanation.surface: A setter reflecting on himself and those who do his puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder, so a muse is a spell of thought or reflection.

clue.text: Property concerning alcohol, say

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
ale is an alcoholic drink
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A document about some drink, as a remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, i.e. property in the legal sense.

clue.text: Masochist remains lost about Fresh Meat, for example

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are rearranged
lost means these letters go missing from the word before

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A masochist's remains go missing around some fresh meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes A, S and H out of MASOCHIST, leaving MOCIST, which 'about' rearranges. Fresh Meat was a British TV comedy about students.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh Meat is an example of a situation comedy on British television.

clue.text: Goes beyond target by means of this shot

parts.note: over can mean via, as in talking over the phone

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A player overshoots the target with this stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhit is to strike too hard, sending the ball past the intended spot.

clue.text: Joined one round point

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the joined pair is read backwards

parts.note: met means came together or joined
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Joined one round point, like assembling a geometric figure.
explanation.walkthrough: MET plus I gives METI, which 'round' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single point or entry on a list or agenda.

clue.text: Roger this then stop talking?

parts.note: roger is radio slang for message received; the clue describes the sign-off used to end a radio exchange

explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a name, but it is the radio word for understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say this phrase to mean their turn is done and the conversation is closed.

clue.text: Destroy Que Sera Sera, but not all of it

indicators.note: only part of the song title is used, so the letters lie inside it

explanation.surface: A demand to wipe out part of the song Que Sera Sera.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or obliterate, to destroy a record.

clue.text: Austerity invited by cities involved in dodgy scam

indicators.note: in places the second set of letters inside the first
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are rearranged
involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed up too

explanation.surface: Belt-tightening invited by towns caught up in a crooked swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals work here: 'dodgy' on the swindle and 'involved' on the towns, the second set nesting between the last two letters of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Asceticism is severe self-denial, an austere way of living.

clue.text: Rubbish covered by foreign articles in drawers

indicators.note: in a down clue being covered by means coming below

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article
pants is British slang for rubbish, as in that film was pants

explanation.surface: Garbage concealed under foreign items in a chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers is an old word for underwear, the garment worn under trousers.

clue.text: New voice for people of Kerala

definitions.note: plural, a community of people; the answer names that caste as a group

parts.note: to air an opinion is to voice it

explanation.surface: A fresh voice for the inhabitants of a south Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nairs are a Hindu caste community of Kerala in southern India.

clue.text: Losing it, violent Asiatic patriarch

indicators.note: violent means wildly disturbed, so these letters are thrown about
losing means the following letters are dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Losing his temper, a violent Asian elder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' drops IT from ASIATIC, leaving ASIAC, which 'violent' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac, son of Abraham, is one of the three biblical patriarchs of Israel.

clue.text: Helen's mum takes first place, shifting daughter

indicators.note: shifting means the letter for daughter moves elsewhere in the word

parts.note: to lead is to be in front

explanation.surface: Helen's mother comes first, moving her daughter about.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the usual abbreviation for daughter; 'shifting' moves it from the end of LEAD to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leda, seduced by Zeus as a swan, was the mother of Helen of Troy.

clue.text: Once irritable, I shrivel up

indicators.note: up means stirred or in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumpy old person complains that they are shrivelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a direction for a down clue, but here it signals the letters of I SHRIVEL are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverish, from an old belief about a bad liver, is a rather dated word for grumpy or peevish.

clue.text: Good luck flower, every bit of it?

definitions.meaning: the flower of something is its finest part, so all of the flower is the whole of the finest

explanation.walkthrough: Flower looks botanical, but it is the sense the pick or finest part.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is a common farewell wishing someone success, and literally the whole of the finest.

clue.text: Dry, about to split old bracket

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the dry letters go round the split

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking, i.e. dry
to rive is an old word for to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A dry old wooden support is about to crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivet is a three-legged stand or bracket for holding a pot over a fire.

clue.text: Note endlessly reflected love, for example

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the shortened note is read backwards
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A love note reflected on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last E from BREVE, giving BREV, which 'reflected' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Love can be an action word, as in to love someone, so it is an example of that part of speech.

clue.text: Equipment submerged in wild water

indicators.note: submerged in means sunk inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: irate means furious, i.e. wild
a rig is a set of equipment, such as a drilling rig

explanation.surface: Gear lost beneath stormy seas.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to water land by channels or sprinklers.

clue.text: A satellite needing section of warhead

indicators.note: section of means only a part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A satellite requires part of a missile's warhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhea is the second-largest moon of Saturn.

clue.text: Blockade now supplying port

indicators.note: supplying means these words provide the letters from within them

explanation.surface: A naval blockade is now feeding a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Behold preliminary survey right away

indicators.note: away means the right letter is removed

parts.note: a recce, short for reconnaissance, is a preliminary look

explanation.surface: Look at a scouting report, right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes the first R from RECCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecce is Latin for behold, as in Ecce Homo.

clue.text: Run to fill pinkish-red pen

indicators.note: to fill means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-red colour
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Running out to fill a pinkish-red fountain pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure for livestock, a pen.

clue.text: Judges restraining a state's testimonials

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the judges go round the state

parts.note: referees judge games
NC is the abbreviation for North Carolina, a US state

explanation.surface: Judges hold back a state's written character statements.
explanation.definitionFit: References are letters vouching for someone's character, i.e. testimonials.

clue.text: Hindu custom revealed by short French composer

indicators.note: short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

explanation.surface: A Hindu custom revealed by a brief French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sati was the former practice of a widow burning herself on her husband's pyre.
